subject: Discovery recap: FinBot inference costs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia@finbot.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: FinBot inference costs & next steps

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap of what we heard and next steps from Redwood's side:

Pain points & goals:
- Primary pain: inference unit economics — embeddings + chat costs are ballooning as usage scales. Current spend up ~3x YoY.
- Success criteria: Reduce per-embed and per-token cost by ~40% without degrading latency beyond ~100–150ms P50 for user-facing calls.
- Other constraints: Data residency in US, SOC2 evidence required, engineering prefers minimal changes to current inference flow.

Current stack you described:
- Model: Llama2-13B (quantized) in self-hosted on AWS (SageMaker endpoints + spot instances)
- Traffic: mix of synchronous chat and batched embedding generation; ~120M tokens/month; peak concurrency ~150 req/s
- Caching: some prefix caching in-house but limited; no global KV-store for embeddings

What Redwood can help with (high level):
- Intelligent batching + async workers for bulk embedding jobs to reduce unit cost
- Prefix/KV caching for chat to cut repeated token generation
- Quantization-friendly runtime and kernel selection to improve throughput on current GPUs

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) You to share traffic distribution / sample payloads and the CSV of inference calls (Sofia said she'll send).
2) Redwood to run a rough unit-cost model and provide a baseline for hosted vs. dedicated pricing.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with engineering to validate latency SLOs and quantization tolerance.

Requested deliverables from Redwood by EOW (Friday): unit-cost model + a short list of questions for the tech call.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-params.xlsx (we'll use to run our model). I'll await the CSV from Sofia.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia@finbot.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinBot inference costs & next steps

Thanks Marissa — that's a great summary.

I've attached the CSV (finbot-inference-distribution.csv) with token-level distribution and request types. A few clarifications:
- About 65% of tokens are embedding requests (short context) processed as batch jobs; 35% are chat requests with variable prefixes.
- Latency SLO: for chat we ideally need P50 < 120ms and P95 < 400ms; embeddings can be async but we have some near-real-time embedding needs with 2–3s acceptable latency.
- We're open to stronger quantization (8-bit / 4-bit) if it doesn't cause unacceptable semantic drift — engineering can validate.

We'd prefer a proposal that shows both hosted and dedicated pricing, and a migration plan that minimizes risk.

Available for tech call Wed or Thu (10–2 PST). Sofia will coordinate.

—
Alex Turner
Head of ML Engineering
FinBot
alex.turner@finbot.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 18:12:00 -0700

Looping you both in — FinBot (Alex + Sofia) just sent the distribution CSV and asked for hosted vs dedicated pricing and a migration plan.

Can you:
- Ben: run the unit-cost model with the attached pricing params (redwood-pricing-params.xlsx) and the finbot CSV once Sofia posts it. Aim to show per-embed and per-token costs for hosted vs reserved/dedicated (include 6/12-mo commit tiers).
- Dylan: prep a short tech-call agenda and a list of validation experiments for quantization tolerance (8-bit vs 4-bit) and caching/batching config. Also confirm latency expectations—P50 <120ms P95 <400ms—and check which GPU families meet that under our runtime.

Target: internal prep by Wed EOD, client tech-call Thu 10–2 PST window. I'll book the slot once you confirm.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-params.xlsx (same)

Thanks —
Marissa
